fields.meta_title: Donor Survey Builder for Nonprofits | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a donor survey that learns how donors want to hear from you, why lapsed donors left, and what first-time donors care about.
fields.h1: Build a Donor Survey That Keeps Donors Giving
fields.hero_description: Build a donor survey that shows why people give, why some stop, and how each donor wants to hear from you.
fields.features_heading: What Your Donor Survey Can Do
fields.features_subheading: Donors see the first two features when they open the link. The other four belong to the development team that reads the answers.
fields.feature_1:
Questions in the donor's own terms

Tell Emergent who gave and what to learn, and it writes each question. A monthly donor rates what their gift pays for, and a first-time donor writes in why they gave.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

A donor who opens the email link on a phone sees one question at a time. Scales take a single tap, and the write-in box comes last, so a busy donor still scores every item.
fields.feature_3:
A contact choice saved to each donor

Ask which channel a donor prefers and the answer is stored on their record. Filter by it before a mailing, and the print list holds only the people who asked for paper.
fields.feature_4:
An email to the gift officer when it matters

Set a rule on any answer, such as a request to visit or a low score from a major donor. The app emails the gift officer who owns that donor the moment the survey comes in.
fields.feature_5:
Answers next to giving history

Responses land in a database you own, beside each donor's first gift and giving level. Connect it by API to the donor CRM your team already uses, and the answers sync.
fields.feature_6:
The survey app, exported to GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the whole survey app to your GitHub repository, with its logic and the results dashboard. Your developer can review or extend it there.

fields.tab_content_1:
Email wins with 214 donors, and print keeps 97

Lantern Hill Food Bank emails its annual donor survey to 1,240 donors, and 386 answer. Asked which channel they prefer, 214 pick email, 97 the print newsletter, 43 text, and 32 a phone call. Development director Corinne Abernathy now mails the newsletter only to those 97.
fields.tab_content_2:
21 lapsed donors who never heard what gifts paid for

Marrow Creek Arts Council sends a 3-question survey to the 310 donors who gave in 2024 but not in 2025, and 58 of them answer. Asked why they stopped, 21 say they never heard what their gift paid for. Another 17 say their budget changed, 12 now give to a different cause, and 8 pick other.
fields.tab_content_3:
Lowell Ashby learns of a rehearsal visit within the day

Every first gift to Ironwood Youth Orchestra is followed by a 4-question welcome survey. Anneliese Moraga writes that her son plays cello and ticks that she would like to visit a rehearsal. When she submits, the app emails her answers to development officer Lowell Ashby, who calls her that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_4:
After clinic photos, monthly donors score 4.1 instead of 3.2

Each spring, Gullwing Wildlife Rescue asks its 140 monthly donors how well they know what their gift pays for, on a 1-5 scale. The 2025 average was 3.2. After a year of monthly clinic photos, 96 donors answer in 2026 and the average is 4.1. Monthly giving manager Rafael Quintero takes it to the board.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Donor Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a donor survey, build it with Emergent, and turn what donors say into changes they notice.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pull in each donor's giving history
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep scored questions on one scale
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the choice the answers will settle, such as which donors still get a printed newsletter. Then cut every question that does not feed it. Share that one decision with your executive director before anyone drafts a question.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Say who answers, when they get the link, and what the results page should count. From that description, Emergent builds the survey along with its database and dashboard. To change a question later, type the change and Emergent updates it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Load first gift date, last gift date, and giving level from your donor records before you send. Then read the results by those fields, and compare first-year donors with donors who have given for 10 years.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use a 1-5 scale for every rated question. This year's averages then line up with next year's. Put one optional write-in question at the end, where skipping it costs you none of the scores.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to three donors you know well, such as a board member, a monthly donor, and a recent first-time donor. Watch one answer on a phone. Reword any question they pause on, and trim the survey if it runs past 4 minutes.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Email each donor a personal link that ties the answer to one record. After 7 days, send one reminder to donors whose answers are still missing. Those who already answered get no further email.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Within 6 weeks, write back to everyone you surveyed. Name one change their answers led to, such as moving the newsletter to email for those who asked. Give the date of the next survey in the same note.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions to ask in a donor survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions to ask in a donor survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions to ask in a donor survey?

faq_plan.a: Ask what made each person give the first time and whether they understand what their gift funds. Then ask how they want to hear from you and whether they plan to give again next year. Good donor survey questions each point to a change your team can make, such as moving a donor from print to email.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a donor survey?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI survey builder who will answer and what you need to learn, in plain English. It builds the donor survey with a database for the answers and a dashboard that counts them. To change a question afterward, type what you want different and Emergent updates the survey.

faq_plan.q: Is there a donor survey template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes: describe the survey you want to Emergent, and the first draft it builds becomes your donor survey template. Reword or cut any question by prompting before you send it. The free tier covers building and publishing. Try the draft on a few donors before it goes to everyone.

faq_plan.q: What are some donor survey examples for different kinds of donors?
faq_plan.a: Four useful donor survey examples each serve one group. Run an annual survey of every donor, a survey of donors who stopped giving, a welcome survey after a first gift, and a yearly check with monthly donors. Schools that raise money from families can add giving questions to a parent survey instead of sending a separate one.

faq_plan.q: How do donor surveys help with fundraising?
faq_plan.hint: How to create donor surveys that improve your fundraising?
faq_plan.a: They tell you why people give and what would keep them giving, which gift records alone cannot show. Act on one answer that donors will notice, such as how often they hear about the work their gifts fund. Emergent sets no response caps, which lets you survey every donor on your list instead of a sample.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a donor survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep an annual donor survey to 10 questions or fewer, and a survey sent right after a gift to 3 or 4. Put the rated questions first and one optional write-in last. If a test donor needs more than 4 minutes on a phone, cut questions until they finish within it.

faq_plan.q: How do I survey donors who are also members?
faq_plan.a: Send them one survey that branches, and keep the two sets of questions apart. Ask members about the benefits they receive in a membership survey, and keep the donor survey on the cause and how gifts are used. Mark who holds a membership in your records, and the survey shows the member questions only to them.

faq_plan.q: Should a donor survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Not by default. A named survey ties each answer to giving history and lets a gift officer follow up with a donor who asks for a visit. Make it anonymous only for sensitive topics, such as how staff treated them, and say so on the first screen. Named answers live in a database you own, next to each donor's record.

faq_plan.q: When is a good time to run a donor survey?
faq_plan.a: Send it when the answers can still change something: within a week of a first gift, or a few months before you plan next year's appeals. Keep it out of the same week as an appeal letter, and send the survey on its own with no ask attached.

faq_plan.q: Can a donor survey cover a fundraising event?
faq_plan.a: It can, but the event is better served by a survey of its own. Send a short post event survey within 2 days that asks about the evening itself, and save questions about giving for the yearly survey. Tag event guests in your donor records, and the yearly results can be split by who attended.

plan.angle: The donor survey SERP is question lists and template galleries from survey tools and fundraising blogs; none shows what a development team does with the answers. This page is for the nonprofit development director who wants to keep donors giving: four organizations each run one donor survey (an annual survey that sets how each donor hears from them, a survey of donors who stopped giving, a welcome survey after a first gift that alerts the gift officer, a yearly check with monthly donors that tracks whether they know what their gift pays for), with real numbers, then question, length, timing and anonymity advice in the FAQ. It stays off the donation form (collecting gifts) and the landing page (asking for gifts): this page is about listening to people who already gave.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Donor Survey That Keeps Donors Giving'; hero 'Build a donor survey that shows why people give, why some stop, and how each donor wants to hear from you.'; how-to description one sentence on what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: PAA 'What are some good questions to ask in a donor survey?' answered first; four worked donor surveys (annual, lapsed, first-gift welcome, monthly donor check), template and examples FAQs, 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Development-team vocabulary throughout: 'gift officer', 'giving level', 'lapsed donors', 'monthly giving manager', 'print list holds only the people who asked for paper'.

openers.evidence: Tabs open on full sentences: 'Lantern Hill Food Bank emails its annual donor survey to 1,240 donors', 'Every first gift to Ironwood Youth Orchestra is followed by a 4-question welcome survey'.

craft.evidence: Two ', so' endings (why_description, feature_2) are within the limit; recorded as a note.

voice.evidence: Concrete scenes and numbers ('Development director Corinne Abernathy now mails the newsletter only to those 97'); no hype verbs or summary sentences.

truth.evidence: domain_sources is empty, yet two sentences state donor behaviour as fact: faq item 9 'A survey that arrives next to a request for money reads like part of the ask.' and feature_2 'Donors open the email link on a phone and see one question at a time.' Numbers otherwise add up (214+97+43+32=386; 21+17+12+8=58); Emergent claims map to claims_used.

distinct.evidence: Page is about listening to people who already gave ('why lapsed donors left'), not collecting or asking for gifts, so it stays off donation-form and nonprofit-landing-page; siblings parent, membership and post event survey are linked, not targeted.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, paa --spec 10 pass / 0 reject / 0 flag; hub link in item 2; links to parent-survey, membership-survey, post-event-survey; no brand or file-format asks.
